title: "Part 3 – Reproduction and exploration"

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/housing-one-day.html#/part-3-reproduction-and-exploration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 3 has two hands-on tasks, the reproduction and a first exploration of the menu of alternatives, with the talk that connects them in between.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, Part 3 | The instruction of Task 2 of Multi100 read word for word, what it left open, and the aim of the reproduction: the chi-square test that analyst 8PTRZ ran on the public file of the original authors (OAs). | 10 minutes |
| Task 3 in your report or working script, or [Browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction) Task 3 | Read the public file `audit_original.csv`, keep the replies that carry a greeting code, mark the Hispanic names, build the two-by-two table and pass it to `chisq.test()`. It should give $\chi^2$ = 14.265 on 558 replies, the value that Multi100 recorded for 8PTRZ. Everyone types their value without sending it and sends it when the facilitator says go, so that the identical values appear at the same moment. | 20 minutes |
| Slides, the continuity correction | Why your number is exactly that number: for a two-by-two table `chisq.test()` applies the continuity correction unless it is told otherwise, and `correct = FALSE` gives 14.95. Then why everyone in the class got the same value while the five analysts, each writing their own code, did not. If you finish early, reproduce the logit of UYV3F, z = −3.771 on 362 replies. | 7 minutes |
| [Specification menu](../../cases/housing/menu.qmd) and slides | The eleven decisions at three levels, the five on which the curve keeps more than one option, the 64 specifications that they make, and the ground rules for the menu: change one decision at a time, and read the reason when an option is refused. | 13 minutes |
| Slides, the methods | A difference in proportions, and the linear probability model against the logit. An optional run of six slides takes the statistics further: odds ratios against percentage points, standard errors for a 0/1 outcome, four tests of one gap, the randomisation test, covariates in an experiment, and the subgroups that sit beside the curve. | 15 minutes |
| Task 4 in the workspace or on the [Browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-4-menu), then [Multiverse](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd) | Call `try_spec()` with no arguments for the reference specification, then three or four times more, changing one argument at a time, and print the tries side by side with `my_experiments()`. Ask once for an option off the curve, such as `model = "three_group"`, to read why it is refused. Then rerun the one that you would defend and send it with `submit_exploration()`. Your mark is drawn on the class chart as an open circle. | 25 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you have reproduced $\chi^2$ = 14.265 yourself and know why it is not 14.95, you have tried three or four alternatives one argument at a time, and you have put an exploratory mark on the class chart.
